rationale: Two actions in one update. First, a correction to the recovery-value family fact: clause (b) said a reply whose value ballot is 'at most' the fabricated one is ignored, which contradicts both the adoption loop's >= test and the measured runs in which peer replies at the same value ballot as the candidate are adopted and one of them replaces the owner's command; the clause now states the strict condition and records that equality is still adopted, which is what clause (d) relies on, and the dependency list the previous revision dropped is restored with current revisions. Second, the experiment request below, which extends the tie-break probe to the three permutations the earlier receipt left unexercised so that the claimed mechanism is checked against all six delivery orders of the same reply set. No measurement or conclusion of the account changes.

scope.description: Owner replica 0 proposes X on its own instance (0,0), replica 1's non-equal pre-accept reply is delivered and replica 1 then fails, so the owner enters the Accept phase at ballot 0 towards replicas 2 and 3; replica 3 accepts without ever pre-accepting (its state holds no command), and the owner's AcceptReplies are left in flight. The owner, alive and still holding X, then runs startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) and the harness delivers the Prepare replies of replicas 2, 3 and 4 (replica 2 carries X at value ballot 0, replicas 3 and 4 carry no command at the same ballot) in a declared order, recording the delivered order, the owner's bookkeeping after the dispatch and what the instance holds afterwards. The six runs cover every permutation of the three peer replies: 2,4,3; 3,4,2; 3,2,4 (recorded by the earlier receipt) and the three added here, 2,3,4; 4,2,3; 4,3,2.
assumptions: Same construction, transport boundary and crash model as the other experiments in this harness.
Delivery order among the prepare replies is chosen by the harness, which is what a real network does not fix; the read order is not altered.
No production logic is modified; the added runs use the same scenario and the same compared field as the earlier three.
The scenario is unchanged from the receipt these runs extend, so the six runs together enumerate the whole permutation space of this reply set.
excluded: No client path, no state-machine execution, no run() loop or recovery timer loop.
No delivery order in which a fourth peer reply exists, which this scenario cannot produce because the accept wave covers two peers and replica 1 has failed.

experiment.prefix: The harness drives the owner's proposal and accept phase through the target's own handlers, fails replica 1 after its reply, delivers the Accept to replicas 2 and 3, then calls the owner's startRecoveryForInstance(0,0). Each recipient's messages are collected before delivery and then delivered in the order declared for that run, with the delivered order recorded, and each run records the owner's leader-bookkeeping state (status, appended count, candidate command length, prepared flag) after the deliveries, the command the owner proposes afterwards and the instance's command list and status.
experiment.requirement: A recovery of an instance must not drop the instance's command when a reply without a command arrives at the same value ballot as replies that carry one, and the adopted value must not depend on the delivery order of equally admissible replies.
experiment.responsibility: The recovering replica's own adoption loop and sub-case dispatch (epaxos/epaxos.go:1236-1313): the replies are the acceptors' honest answers at their stored ballots and the harness only chooses the arrival order.

comparisons.description: Run D (replies 2,3,4): the command-carrying reply is delivered first while an empty reply is adopted at the trigger position, so a violated outcome adds a third order in which the loss follows the trigger position and not the reply content.
Run E (replies 4,2,3): an empty reply is delivered first while the command-carrying reply is adopted at the trigger position, so the instance is expected to keep the owner's command.

Run F (replies 4,3,2): both replies delivered before the trigger carry nothing and the command-carrying reply arrives last, so a violated outcome shows the trigger prefix decides and the reply that follows it cannot restore the command.

experiment.revision_reason: Added the three remaining permutations of the three-reply tie set (2,3,4; 4,2,3; 4,3,2) to the same test, so the single receipt covers all six orders. Scenario, handlers, crash point and compared fields are unchanged from the earlier revision of this test.

knowledge.statement: In the captured EPaxos package the value a recovery adopts is not protected by the quorum that holds it: four distinct mechanisms of the same recovery path each let a recovering replica end up proposing, and then deciding, a value other than the one its prepare replies carry. (a) startRecoveryForInstance fabricates a value ballot for its own empty state, so the adoption loop skips genuine replies (epaxos/epaxos.go:1145-1165, 1239-1246). (b) A reply whose value ballot is below the running candidate ballot - which begins at the recoverer's pre-recovery local value ballot and rises to the fabricated recovery ballot as the loop adopts - is ignored even when it reports the highest accepted value, so a NOOP replaces an accepted value, including one another live replica has already committed; a reply whose value ballot equals the running candidate is still adopted, which is what lets an empty reply replace the command in (d). (c) A reply that reports the instance COMMITTED is discarded once its status reaches lb.status, because the pre-accept guard then rejects the remaining replies, so the first recovery attempt stalls until the retry (epaxos/epaxos.go:870-881, 1255-1313). (d) A reply that carries no command decodes as a non-nil empty slice, which the sub-case 5/6 fallback passes to startPhase1 instead of state.NOOP() (epaxos/defs.go:228-235, epaxos/epaxos.go:1307-1311), and the adopted value is the one carried by the last reply appended before the appended count reaches SlowQuorumSize - the fabricated self reply counts toward that threshold, so the trigger falls on the second delivered peer reply and the dispatch then replaces the bookkeeping, so replies delivered afterwards cannot restore the command; the owner's command therefore survives exactly when that second peer reply carries it, measured on one fixed reply set with two command-carrying and two empty peer replies as kept for the orders 1,2,3,4 and 3,1,4,2 and dropped for 1,3,4,2 and 3,4,1,2. Recovering replicas that already hold the value are not affected by (a)-(b), and the client re-offer protects the single-NOOP case but not the empty-slice case.
knowledge.conditions: N=5, F=2 configuration of the captured snapshot with Thrifty on and IsLeader false at the recovering replica; the instance owner fails inside its accept window and the recovering replica holds the instance without its command, or (for the arrival-order variant) recovers its own instance while replies at the same value ballot differ.

knowledge.assertion: empty slice adopted and passed through, with the reply at the slow-quorum trigger position deciding the command
COMMITTED status adopted then later replies discarded
a recovery lacking the command can decide a different value than a live replica's committed value
